tier_reason: Tier A stands on reproducibility (public benches, Rust 1.62, clang 13, stated CPUs), but the enricher's reading of the harness removes two rows and corrects the count: the 'Fill All' test compares tiny-skia's Pixmap::fill overwrite with cairo's paint() alpha blend (and Skia's draw_color blend), so its 5.1x x86 and 62x ARM wins are invalid; the 'Destination' operator is a no-op; the bicubic row compares cairo Filter::Best with tiny-skia bicubic (different filters, 11.9x). Recount against cairo on x86 AVX2: 37 of 46 tests, geometric mean 2.24x; without Fill All and Destination 36 of 44 at 2.32x; the default SSE2 build 34 of 44 at 1.71x (derived from page data). On the M1 run cairo's times are 4.9-8.3x worse than on the 3700X for basic fills while Skia is unchanged, consistent with a pixman build without NEON (search snippet only; the ARM cairo build is undocumented). Skia was handicapped with SK_FORCE_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLITTER, and the 2021 benches README says Skia v85 while the build steps check out m90.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 20-100% slower than Skia on x86-64 and about 100-300% slower on ARM, 'still faster than cairo and raqote in many cases'. Results pages (gh-pages x86_64.html, July 2021; arm.html, Aug 2022), excluding the invalid Fill All (overwrite versus blend) and no-op Destination rows: tiny-skia AVX2 beats cairo in 36 of 44 x86 tests (geometric mean 2.32x; the default SSE2 build 34 of 44 at 1.71x) and beats cairo in most ARM tests, where cairo's build appears to lack NEON (derived from page data). Cairo wins on x86 rect fills (0.37-0.45x), Nearest pattern (0.39x) and Source Over/Destination Over/Plus blending (0.31-0.58x); tiny-skia wins most on non-separable blend modes (4.5-9x) and AA hairlines (4.4x); the bicubic 11.9x compares different filters (cairo Best). Against Skia AVX2 tiny-skia wins only 5 of 50 x86 tests.
